findings.quote: James H. Litinsky, the company's founder, serves as Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer.
findings.issue: The grounding surface does not state that Litinsky founded MP Materials. The company description (Context) says only "MP Materials Corp. was founded in 2017" without naming a founder, and the proxy excerpt gives his title solely as "Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer." "the company's founder" is a recalled/unsupported executive attribution. It recurs and carries the equity story: leadership also says "The business is founder-led"; governance says "founder James Litinsky, as Chairman and CEO, is not" [independent]; insiderOwnership says "founder and CEO James Litinsky beneficially owned 12,809,732 shares."
findings.fix: Remove "founder"/"founder-led" everywhere it appears (leadership, governance, insiderOwnership) unless the proxy or Context supports it. Refer to Litinsky by his grounded title (Chairman and CEO) and keep the leadership-concentration point on the Chair+CEO combination, which the proxy does support.
findings.note: Fixed. "founder"/"founder-led" removed throughout: leadership now opens "James H. Litinsky serves as Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer"; governance reads "James Litinsky, as Chairman and CEO, is not"; insiderOwnership reads "Chairman and CEO James Litinsky." No occurrence of "founder" remains in the built report.

findings.quote: Among disclosed holders, Hancock Prospecting Pty Limited held 7.8% and The Vanguard Group 7.7%, with ownership otherwise dispersed among institutions. The presence of a strategic industrial holder alongside index funds and the founder gives the register a mix of long-term and passive capital rather than a single controlling block.
findings.issue: Vanguard 7.7% is presented as a current holder and an "index funds ... passive capital" reading is built on it, but the same proxy's footnote (2) states that per Vanguard's most recent Schedule 13G/A (filed March 27, 2026) it "beneficially owns 0.0% as of March 13, 2026 following an internal reorganization pursuant to which The Vanguard Group's beneficial ownership has been disaggregated." The 7.7% derives from a 13G/A as of December 29, 2023 and is superseded — the report silently picks the stale figure (source disagreement not disclosed) and dates it as current. Hancock's 7.8% is likewise as of September 30, 2024 per footnote (1) and is left undated. "strategic industrial holder" is not on the surface.
findings.fix: State that Vanguard's most recent 13G/A (March 27, 2026) reports 0.0% as of March 13, 2026 after disaggregation, and either drop Vanguard from the register or name the disagreement and which figure you use. Date Hancock's 7.8% (as of September 30, 2024). Drop the ungrounded "strategic industrial holder" characterization or replace it with what the proxy carries.
findings.note: Fixed. The stale Vanguard 7.7% and Hancock 7.8% figures and the ungrounded "strategic industrial holder"/"index funds" framing are gone. insiderOwnership now keeps only the grounded, dated Litinsky 7.2% (as of April 13, 2026) and states "The rest of the register is dispersed among institutional holders, with no single outside party holding a controlling block" — supported by the proxy and free of the superseded figure.

findings.quote: Revenue in the second quarter of 2026 was $108.5 million, up 89% from a year earlier
findings.issue: Cross-section repetition. This sentence appears verbatim in both sections.executiveSummary.thesis.body and sections.financials.incomeCommentary. Other figures are retold across sections: the full consensus-target set ($74.29 / +50.7% / median $75.00 / range $57.00-$100.00) near-verbatim in analystCommentary and sections.valuation.multiplesCommentary; Q2 operating margin -29.5% in thesis, incomeCommentary and risks.idiosyncratic[0]; FY2025 FCF -$328.1M in cashflowCommentary and risks.idiosyncratic[0]; FY2025 capex $172.4M in cashflowCommentary and management.capitalAllocation; "$49.30 ... half its 52-week high of $100.25" in thesis, multiplesCommentary and finalRecommendation[0]; magnet capacity 3,000/7,000/10,000 MT near-verbatim in catalysts and growth.points.
findings.fix: Introduce each figure once in its home section and refer back in words elsewhere. The executive summary and analyst preamble should point; the sections argue. Delete the duplicated sentences (especially the verbatim Q2 revenue line and the repeated consensus-target set).
findings.note: Fixed. Each flagged figure now has a single home: $108.5M only in incomeCommentary (thesis points with "Revenue grew 89%"); consensus-target set only in analystCommentary (multiplesCommentary now "Analysts' price targets sit well above the current price"); -29.5% only in incomeCommentary; -$328.1M only in cashflowCommentary (risks says "burned free cash flow"); $172.4M only in cashflowCommentary (capitalAllocation says "heavy"); $100.25 only in thesis (referred to in words elsewhere); the 3,000/7,000 breakdown only in growth.points (catalyst points with "roughly 10,000").

findings.quote: Standard committee independence and related-party review are in place.
findings.issue: Over-attribution. The captured proxy excerpt covers only director and committee independence (the "Director Independence" section and the audit/compensation/nominating committee determinations); it does not carry any related-party transaction review. Asserting that "related-party review" is in place characterises the proxy with something it does not contain on the surface.
findings.fix: Drop the related-party clause, or limit the sentence to what the proxy excerpt supports — the board's independence determinations and that the audit, compensation and nominating committees are composed of independent directors.
findings.note: Fixed. The "related-party review" sentence is removed. governance now closes on the Chair/CEO-concentration point and retains only the grounded independence determinations (six named independent directors; audit, compensation and nominating committees composed of independent directors).

findings.quote: The shares fall back toward the low end of their range.
findings.issue: The Bear driver says the shares fall "toward the low end of their range," but the Bear implied price of $32 sits below the 52-week low of $37.81 that is on the surface, so it pierces the range rather than approaching its low end. Minor prose/number inconsistency in the calls.
findings.fix: Reword to reflect that the bear case takes the shares below the 52-week low (e.g. "below the bottom of its 52-week range"), or otherwise align the language with the $32 figure.
findings.note: Fixed. The Bear driver now ends "The shares fall sharply from current levels," which is consistent with the $32 implied price (a sharp fall from $49.30) and no longer mischaracterises it as merely approaching the low end of the range.

findings.quote: supply and pricing are heavily influenced by China, which dominates global rare-earth processing and has used export controls as a policy tool.
findings.issue: "dominates global rare-earth processing" states a market-share fact not on the grounding surface. The MD&A establishes only that China imposed and expanded rare-earth export controls in 2025 (suspended in November 2025) and that customers are seeking supply outside China — not that China "dominates global rare-earth processing."
findings.fix: Frame China's role with what the pack supports (the 2025 export controls, the November 2025 suspension, and demand shifting to non-Chinese supply) and drop the ungrounded "dominates global rare-earth processing" claim.
findings.note: Fixed. systemic now reads "heavily influenced by China, which imposed and expanded rare-earth export controls in 2025 and can use them as a policy tool" — grounded in the MD&A. The ungrounded "dominates global rare-earth processing" claim is gone.
